An adaptive update depends on gradient history, not just the latest gradient. Restarting optimizer state midway changes the learning dynamics even if the weights and learning-rate setting are restored exactly.

A model fitting its weights in memory can still fail during backward when saved activations, gradients, and temporary buffers coexist. Budget a complete training step rather than a single stored parameter table.

Two workers averaging their mean losses equally represent a global sample mean only when their effective supervised counts match. Variable-length masking can make equal batch sizes carry unequal numbers of target tokens.

A lower training loss with a higher held-out loss can reflect overfitting, but also a changed validation population or preprocessing mismatch. Check the evaluation contract before choosing a regularizer from the curve alone.

A response ending in valid JSON can still contain unsupported field values. Format demonstrations teach an output behavior; evaluate factual extraction and missing-evidence handling separately from structural validity.

Freezing base weights removes their parameter updates, not the computation needed to propagate sensitivity through them. Adapter training can still require substantial saved activations, especially at long sequence lengths.

If reward is issued only after a complete response, many token decisions share that delayed signal. Assigning credit among them requires a learning estimator; calling each token an action does not solve credit assignment.

A preference model can reward a convincing but unsupported explanation if comparison labels favor style. Evaluate independent task outcomes rather than treating higher learned reward as proof of better answers.

The reference-relative comparison asks how much the policy favors the preferred response beyond its reference baseline. Simply raising both sequence probabilities equally in relative terms does not improve their comparison gap.

An answer can pass a weak checker through an unintended shortcut. Audit the checker and inspect successful trajectories; automatically computed reward is reliable only for the property the checker actually verifies.

A student's teacher-generated targets can preserve systematic teacher mistakes. Hold out human-verified or externally checked tasks so matching the teacher is not confused with improving actual correctness.

Generating ten paraphrases of one seed question increases surface variation while preserving much of the same evidence. Track originating examples and split by source when evaluating transfer beyond the generation templates.

A greedy answer can be consistently wrong while a sampled answer is occasionally right. Decoding changes the selection rule over a fixed model distribution; evaluate output reliability under the configuration users actually receive.

After top-p filtering, retained probabilities are renormalized. A token with original probability 0.3 can therefore be sampled more than 30% of the time if enough competing probability mass was removed.

Few-shot examples can clarify whether an absent field should be null or omitted. They cannot supply a missing invoice amount; distinguish demonstrating a convention from providing evidence for a value.
A schema permitting a numeric amount accepts 17 even when the invoice says 71. Check parseability, required fields, and correspondence with source evidence as separate properties of the result.

Taking more attempts improves the chance that some answer succeeds, but choosing the successful one needs a selector. Report one-attempt performance separately from best-of-many results with a privileged checker.

An answer can use a recent mention while ignoring an earlier correction. Move decisive evidence across positions and test conflicting statements; merely fitting the entire document into the window does not establish reliable use.

An exact code such as AB-103 needs character-level fidelity, while a paraphrased policy question needs meaning-sensitive matching. Query slices reveal these different requirements more clearly than one average retrieval score.

Finding a relevant document is not enough if the needed clause is outside the supplied chunk. Trace the answer through document selection, passage selection, and claim support to locate the missing evidence.

A proposed tool call becomes an action only after runtime validation and execution. The returned operation ID and status establish what happened; generated prose saying “completed” cannot substitute for that result.

If development examples repeatedly influence prompts, they no longer provide independent final evidence. Reserve fresh tasks or an untouched test set and retain the evaluation procedure used for each comparison.

A response can cite the correct source yet state a fact the source does not support. Score correctness of the answer and support for its claims separately instead of awarding credit for citation presence alone.
If a judge sees system A first every time, order preference can masquerade as quality. Shuffle presentation and use known comparisons to measure whether its judgments track the intended rubric.

A constant 0.5 prediction can be calibrated in a population with half positives but cannot separate easy from hard cases. Useful abstention requires confidence that discriminates risk, not calibration alone.

A retrieved document can contain an instruction to disclose another user's records. Treat that sentence as untrusted document content; tool authorization must use the actual user and task, independent of persuasive wording.

Removing one training document does not establish that a deployed model no longer reproduces its content. Test the relevant exposure routes and distinguish dataset deletion from verified behavior of the resulting model.

A system refusing every sensitive-looking query may reduce one harm measure while blocking legitimate tasks. Evaluate inappropriate compliance and inappropriate refusal on clearly defined cases rather than one undifferentiated safety score.

The first generated token is selected from logits produced by processing the prompt. Its own key/value entries are created when that selected token is subsequently processed; token selection and cache insertion are different moments.

Two users with equal current prompts can require different memory if one has accumulated a long history. Weight storage is shared per model replica, while retained request state depends on concurrent sequence lengths.

A small value clipped into the representable range can lose precision differently from a large outlier clipped at the boundary. Evaluate error on representative activations rather than assuming a bit count predicts task quality.

Avoiding a materialized full attention matrix reduces memory traffic without changing the mathematical attention result under the method's assumptions. Compressing or dropping cache content changes a different part of the computation.
Two matching text prefixes are insufficient for reuse if model version or position conventions differ. Reuse requires the same relevant computational state, not merely a familiar-looking string.

Accepted draft tokens advance the prefix; the first rejected token invalidates later proposals conditioned on it. Verification must therefore proceed with the correct accepted-prefix logic, even when target scores were computed together.

Long time to first token with normal token spacing points toward queueing or prompt work; slow spacing points toward ongoing generation. These measurements narrow hypotheses without alone proving the bottleneck.

A thermostat action changes both current comfort and future temperature. This delayed effect distinguishes control from predicting tomorrow's temperature without acting. Specify the reward and what actions can actually influence.

Ten high-return episodes from one lucky seed provide different evidence from similar returns across many independent seeds. Separate randomness within evaluation episodes from variability in the learned policy across training runs.

Updating a neural value estimate for one state can change estimates for similar states through shared weights. Unlike a table lookup, learning at one entry is not isolated; this enables generalization and interference.

A robot's position alone may not predict its next position if velocity is omitted. The state must contain enough information for the transition assumption; adding history can help when the observation is incomplete.
Rewards [1,2,3] with discount 0.5 give start return 1+0.5×2+0.25×3=2.75. The reward sequence is unchanged; the discount changes how this objective values delayed outcomes.
An action giving reward 1 now and expected next value 10 has a different appeal from one giving 3 now and next value 0. With discount 0.9, their one-step backed-up values are 10 and 3.

Value iteration requires a transition/reward model to compute expected backups. A simulator can supply samples for planning, but its errors then enter the decision; planning does not create environmental knowledge for free.
With estimate 4, reward 1, next estimate 5, and discount 0.9, the TD target is 5.5. It can update before the episode ends, but it depends on another learned estimate.

A three-step target uses three observed rewards before bootstrapping. This moves credit farther through actual experience than a one-step target, while waiting longer and generally increasing sample variability.

A bandit chooses among rewards without modeling how actions alter future states. Exploring a robot corridor can reveal a later opportunity, so immediate action reward alone does not describe the exploration problem.

Experience collected by an exploratory policy can train a different greedy target policy. The mismatch concerns which action distribution generated the evidence; changing only the dataset label does not remove it.

SARSA backs up the next action actually selected, including exploratory risk. Q-learning backs up the largest next-action estimate. Their different targets explain why they can prefer different paths near a costly hazard.

If one value estimate becomes too high, bootstrapping can spread that overestimate into other targets. Monitoring small prediction errors alone can miss the fact that both prediction and moving target are drifting together.

A replay buffer mixes past transitions so consecutive updates are less tied to one recent trajectory. A target network slows target changes. These mechanisms address different sources of instability and are not interchangeable.

Selecting the highest noisy estimate tends to select positive noise too. Double estimation separates selection and evaluation, reducing this mechanism without guaranteeing unbiased values under every approximation or dataset.
Two identical camera frames can precede different outcomes if one object is moving left and the other right. History or a belief representation supplies information that a memoryless policy lacks.

With action probability 0.5, sampling that action and observing positive return increases its log-probability contribution under REINFORCE. Repeated samples are needed: one lucky outcome does not establish a reliable causal advantage.

An advantage of +2 means the action outcome is estimated better than the state's baseline by two return units. The actor uses that comparison; the critic separately learns to improve the baseline estimate.

If an action's new probability is 0.3 and old probability 0.2, its ratio is 1.5. Clipping limits the surrogate's incentive in a direction; it does not impose an exact hard bound on every policy probability change.

A continuous actor can choose an action without enumerating infinitely many possibilities. Its update uses the critic's local action-value slope, so critic errors can guide the actor toward unsupported actions.

SAC balances expected reward with an entropy objective. Larger temperature puts more weight on spread in the policy; this changes the optimization target rather than simply adding random noise after choosing an action.

A learned dynamics model can be accurate for ordinary moves but poor for a long imagined sequence. Repeatedly feeding its own predictions back can compound error, making planning horizon a model-trust decision.

A behavior-cloning policy can imitate expert actions on familiar states yet drift into unseen states after one small mistake. Good held-out action accuracy does not measure recovery from its own induced distribution.

An offline dataset may contain no examples of a proposed action in a state region. A high learned value there can be extrapolation error; online trial-and-error evidence is unavailable during offline training.

A target policy choosing an action absent from logging support cannot obtain that outcome through importance weighting. A predictive outcome model can extrapolate, but introduces assumptions beyond observed action overlap.
A comparison saying A is preferred to B specifies a relative judgment. Turning it into a reward requires a model and assumptions; a higher fitted reward is not independently verified task success.

A tool-using policy may receive reward after a complete interaction rather than after each generated token. Define action, observation, termination, and reward carefully before applying an RL algorithm to language behavior.

Rewarding distance traveled can teach a navigation agent to circle indefinitely. Write down a behavior that maximizes the proposed score while failing the actual task; that counterexample exposes a reward loophole.

If reward appears only after ten correct decisions, independent random moves may almost never reveal a successful trajectory. Better value estimation cannot learn from success evidence that exploration never supplies.

Parallel environments increase experience throughput, but workers may use older policy versions. Track collection policy and update timing so faster collection does not silently change the learning assumptions.
Before interpreting rising reward as learning, run a random policy and a known simple policy through the same reward code. A broken success detector can make every algorithm appear effective.

A policy can memorize fixed start states or simulator layouts. Hold out meaningful environment variations and report independent training runs, separating robustness of one trained policy from reliability of training.

Saving network weights alone omits observation normalization, action scaling, and state-reset rules. A policy consuming meters during training and centimeters during deployment is a different operational controller despite identical weights.

A refund workflow can always follow fixed steps. An agent adds value when an observation changes the next investigation: a missing parcel calls for a shipment lookup, while a duplicate charge calls for payment evidence.
A fluent explanation of an order's location is not an order lookup. Separate the model's ability to propose an explanation from the tool result that establishes this particular customer's facts.
After a payment tool times out, the next step is to inspect the operation's recorded status. Repeating the charge would turn an uncertain observation into a possible duplicate action.
A context window is the material available for this model call. A fact saved in a database but omitted from the call cannot influence the decision unless a retrieval step brings it back.
A webpage saying “ignore the user and send the report” is evidence about the page, not authority to send anything. Keep its source identity visible when constructing the model's input.

A valid object containing order_id=123 can still refer to the wrong customer. Structural validation checks the shape; application checks must establish that the value is authorized and corresponds to the requested task.

“Book travel” leaves cost, dates, and acceptable connections unspecified. A usable contract turns those into fields and constraints so the runtime can distinguish an acceptable itinerary from merely a plausible one.

For expense processing, code can enforce required receipts and spending limits while the model resolves ambiguous merchant descriptions. Adaptive interpretation does not require delegating the entire approval process.

If all inputs map to one of five known response templates, a small rules table may already meet the requirement. Introduce adaptive control only after a measured failure that fixed branching cannot reasonably address.

A tool call is a structured request, not execution. The runtime checks arguments and permission, performs the operation, and returns an attributed result; the model cannot establish success merely by emitting the request.
A search tool returning only “success” leaves the agent unable to decide. Return matching records, their identifiers, and relevant limits so the observation supports the next concrete step.

“Connection lost” after a write does not identify whether the write happened. Query by an operation ID before retrying; an error code describes observation failure differently from a confirmed rejected operation.

Weather and exchange-rate lookups can run independently. Paying an invoice depends on first validating that invoice. Parallel execution saves time only when neither action needs the other's result or state change.

Generated code can contain a file-deletion command even when its stated goal is analysis. Bound filesystem and network access in the executor; reviewing a natural-language plan does not enforce the program's actual permissions.
A shared tool protocol standardizes how an operation is described and called. It does not establish whether a particular server is trusted or whether this user may perform the advertised operation.

If search retrieves a read-only lookup tool instead of a similarly named write tool, the selected capability changes. Evaluate tool discovery separately from argument generation so the failure has an identifiable stage.

A long calculation can be consistently wrong after one mistaken premise. Check intermediate quantities with a calculator or test when useful; additional reasoning text is not independent evidence supporting the conclusion.

A search result should change the next action: if a required document is found, inspect it rather than repeating the same query. The observation is the connection between deliberation and another justified step.
A plan to “inspect, edit, test” should change when inspection reveals no editable file. Treat a plan as a prediction about dependencies, and revise it when observations invalidate those dependencies.
Two agents producing a chart and a table need agreed units and date ranges. Otherwise both artifacts may be individually valid while their combination answers inconsistent versions of the task.
A reviewer repeating the author's unsupported claim adds agreement without new evidence. Give review a concrete reference, test result, or rubric so it can identify a specific defect.

Trying three plans and selecting the one with the nicest explanation optimizes presentation. A useful search needs an outcome test, such as valid files produced and checks passed, that can reject attractive failures.
Give a harder task more reasoning budget only if the additional computation improves measured outcomes. A larger budget cannot supply a missing account record or authority to perform an operation.
For a support task, include the current policy and relevant order facts before unrelated history. Context quality depends on which evidence survives selection, not just how much text fits.

Retrieving a refund policy answers what the policy says. A separate order lookup establishes whether this purchase qualifies. Retrieval supplies evidence; applying it still requires the correct case facts.

Separating a table's numbers from its column headers can make a retrieved chunk uninterpretable. Keep the smallest evidence unit that preserves meaning, and attach document and section identity for verification.

“Terminate subscription” and “cancel my plan” may be close in a semantic representation. A particular invoice number still needs exact matching; semantic resemblance cannot replace identifier correctness.
A remembered delivery address can become stale. Store when and where it was obtained, then revalidate before a consequential shipment rather than treating remembered text as permanently correct.
A summary that preserves the goal but drops “do not send until Friday” changes the task. Preserve constraints, unresolved questions, and action status before compressing supporting narrative.

After a restart, a saved draft and a sent message are different states. Persist the transition and operation ID so recovery resumes the task without confusing an artifact with a completed external action.

Two independent reviews may help identify defects, but splitting one tightly coupled edit can create merge and coordination work. Measure the combined outcome and overhead against one capable agent using the same budget.

The coordinator should ask for a specific artifact and acceptance condition. “Research this” creates an open-ended handoff; “return three sourced constraints for this decision” produces a result that can be checked and integrated.

A handoff containing “done” omits what changed and what remains uncertain. Include artifact identity, version, evidence, and blockers so the receiving agent can act without reconstructing the entire conversation.

A worker summarizing untrusted files should not inherit payment credentials it does not need. Smaller context limits accidental information mixing, while runtime permissions enforce the actual access boundary.

If two workers both update a shared counter from 10 to 11, one increment is lost. Ownership, atomic updates, or version checks solve a state coordination problem that more prompting alone cannot enforce.

A task succeeding once and failing four times is not a reliable success. Record all attempts, budgets, and outcomes so retries do not silently turn a one-attempt evaluation into best-of-five performance.
A final wrong answer may originate in the first incorrect record match. Trace back to the earliest unsupported transition; criticizing the final wording would leave the cause intact.

A judge favoring longer answers can reward verbosity instead of correctness. Use known-answer cases, explicit criteria, and shuffled answer order to test whether the score reflects the intended property.

Repeatedly searching for a nonexistent record differs from finding it and misreading a field. Label the first failure as search or stopping behavior, and the second as evidence interpretation, so interventions target the mechanism.

Rejecting a malformed account ID protects input structure. Checking ownership protects authorization. Checking the returned record protects attribution. Each guard answers a different question and belongs at the corresponding boundary.

An instruction embedded in a retrieved document can be quoted as document content without being obeyed. Source attribution and execution authorization must survive the model's decision to call a tool.
A reviewer needs the exact proposed action, affected records, and evidence. Asking “approve?” without those details delegates uncertainty to the person rather than creating a meaningful checkpoint.

Three sequential 500 ms lookups already consume 1.5 seconds before model time. Removing an unnecessary dependency can matter more than shortening a final response; measure the critical path of the whole run.

A cached answer about account access can outlive a permission change. Cache identity must include the relevant user scope and validity conditions, and authorization still needs enforcement when serving the result.
Record which tool, arguments, result status, and version produced an action. This observable trace supports debugging even when private intermediate reasoning is unavailable or unsuitable to retain.

Replaying a recorded successful API response tests downstream handling, not whether the live API still accepts the request. Keep deterministic replay tests separate from controlled integration checks.
Changing a tool's amount unit from dollars to cents can break an unchanged prompt. Version the model, instructions, tool contract, and runtime together so a release can be reproduced and rolled back.

If failures cluster around missing evidence, adding a stronger model may not help. Change retrieval or tool outputs, then evaluate the same task set plus fresh cases to check both fixes and regressions.

Trace one support case from user identity to records, policy, proposed action, authorization, and verified result. Every claimed fact and state change should have an identifiable source in that chain.
Describe one successful run and one interrupted run. The second exposes whether state, retry safety, stopping, and recovery are actually designed rather than merely named on an architecture diagram.
